title: 3 ingredients for building reliable enterprise agents - Harrison Chase, LangChain/LangGraph
talk_summary: Harrison Chase frames reliable enterprise agents as a value/cost equation and argues for deterministic workflow segments, observability/evals, reversible changes with human approval, and event-triggered ambient agents. The talk is conceptual but gives copyable patterns: agent inboxes, first drafts, and time-travel/resume.

takeaways.what_they_do: Encode mandatory sequences as code/state machines instead of relying on prompts, while still allowing agentic loops where useful.
takeaways.evidence_quote: make more and more of your agent deterministic.

takeaways.what_they_do: Trace every LLM/tool step and benchmark agent behavior against cases so failures are visible and debuggable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can just see every step that's happening inside the agent.

takeaways.technique: Reversible diffs plus human approval gates
takeaways.what_they_do: Make agent changes easy to revert and require human approval before risky actions land.
takeaways.evidence_quote: make it easy to reverse the changes that the agent makes.

takeaways.technique: Event-triggered ambient agents with approval inbox
takeaways.what_they_do: Trigger background agents from events rather than human chat, and surface actions needing approval in an inbox.
takeaways.evidence_quote: ambient agents are triggered by events

takeaways.what_they_do: Have the human calibrate the task upfront, let the agent do bulk work asynchronously, then review key points or a draft.
takeaways.evidence_quote: first drafts I think are a great kind of like mental model for that

takeaways.what_they_do: Checkpoint agent steps so a failed long run can be rewound to the last good step and resumed with a correction.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if it messed up on step like 10 out of 100, you can reverse back to step 10
